Subject: Security KMS & Encryption — Post-call recap and next steps

Hi Samira / David —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap + answers to the KMS/encryption and compliance questions you raised, plus proposed next steps.

Call summary (high level):
- Use case: FinHealth will route sensitive PII/PHI inference traffic to Redwood for summarization and triage.
- Concern areas: SOC 2 evidence and timeline, HIPAA applicability/BAA, encryption at-rest/in-transit, customer-managed keys and HSM support, vendor questionnaire kickoff.

Short answers to the key technical/security questions we covered:
- SOC 2: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type I and is targeting Type II finalization in Q1 2027; attached is a redacted SOC 2 summary (controls, scope). Full report available under NDA.
- GDPR / HIPAA: We support GDPR controls and offer a HIPAA program (BAA available). For PHI workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated deployments; hosted customers can also sign a BAA if the data flows meet your requirements.
- Encryption in transit: All traffic is TLS 1.2+; we recommend TLS 1.3 for new integrations.
- Encryption at rest: Model and customer data at rest are encrypted using AES-256.
- KMS / customer-managed keys (CMK):
  - Hosted: Redwood-managed keys by default via cloud provider KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).
  - Dedicated / Private: Support for BYOK (customer-managed keys) with integration to your KMS/HSM. Keys can remain in your tenant or HSM; Redwood performs envelope encryption and never stores plaintext customer keys.
  - HSM-backed keys: Supported for Private deployments and Dedicated through CloudHSM integrations or customer HSM appliances in a VPC/on-prem setup.
  - Key rotation: Rotation is handled by the customer's KMS for CMKs; Redwood transparently re-encrypts envelopes and preserves availability.
- Audit logs / key usage: Key usage events are surfaced in the Redwood Console and can be exported to your SIEM (CloudTrail, Stackdriver, Azure Monitor). We also provide token-level request logs (redacted for PII) under your retention settings.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf (redacted controls map).

Proposed next steps:
1) I will upload the SOC 2 summary and start the vendor security questionnaire flow — please confirm the best technical contact (David?) and legal contact for the BAA.
2) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min deep-dive with our security/infra engineer to show KMS integration options (we can do a short demo of envelope encryption + CloudHSM).
3) Please upload your vendor questionnaire (or use the DocuSign link I’ll send) and we’ll populate answers and return within ~3 business days for your review.

Happy to jump on a call — what times work for you next week?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Hi David / Samira —

Thanks — answers inline below, and next steps at the bottom. I’ve also started the questionnaire flow and attached the SOC 2 summary for your review.

1) HSM / key custody
- For Private deployments: you can keep keys in your on-prem HSM or cloud HSM and we never import raw key material into Redwood. We support an envelope encryption model where the CEK (content encryption key) is protected by your master key in your HSM/KMS; only ciphertext leaves your environment. That satisfies "sole custody" requirements for most audits. For Dedicated we support CloudHSM integration (you provision and control the HSM).

2) Audit logging
- Key usage events: we surface events with fields like timestamp, key_id (masked), operation (encrypt/decrypt), request_id, instance_id, and service_context. Sample logs can be exported to CloudTrail (AWS), Audit Logs (GCP), or forwarded to Splunk/Datadog via our log export connector. Retention is configurable; default retention is 90 days in the Console, longer retention is available as an add-on.

3) Rotation SLA
- Key rotation is driven by your KMS; when you rotate the CMK, Redwood will detect the new key id and perform re-wrapping of envelopes. Typical re-encryption is streaming and incremental — no downtime for inference traffic in our Dedicated/Private patterns. For hosted flows with Redwood-managed keys we coordinate a maintenance window for customer-visible key rotations.

BAA / SOC2
- Our legal team signs BAAs; please indicate the FinHealth legal contact and we’ll route the BAA for signature. For SOC 2, I’ve linked the redacted SOC2 summary (attached); the full report is available under NDA. I’m cc’ing Neha (security/compliance) and Marissa (sales lead) who will help with the questionnaire responses and any redlines.

Next steps:
- I started the DocuSign questionnaire flow: https://www.docusign.com/s/start/abc123-questionnaire
- Please confirm David as technical owner and Samira as business owner for the questionnaire.
- Neha / Marissa — can you review the SOC2 summary and the draft answers I’ll add to the questionnaire? I’ll ping you with a link to the draft.

If it helps, we can do a 30-min technical session (we’ll include one of our infra engineers) — propose Tue 12/7 10:00–10:30 PST or Wed 12/8 14:00–14:30 PST.
